1791223068.subject: One ruler for items, mob ranks
1791223068.text:
Two big changes at once: every item in the world is now measured on one ruler, and every monster got a rank.

One ruler for every item
Random loot, crafting, quest rewards, enchantments and the sage's advice now count an item's power in the same units. A higher tier means a stronger item, and it counts the same wherever it came from.
- Corpses now drop armor too, twice as often as weapons: head, body, shoulders, hands, legs, feet and shields. Often right into your weakest slot.
- The item is built for whoever made the kill: casters get mana and regeneration, fighters get damage, hitroll and health. It won't repeat what you already wear.
- The sage's advice service measures with the same ruler, so now you can actually trust it.
Details in the help on random items.

Mob ranks
Every monster now has a rank: weakling, ordinary foe, veteran, champion, boss or legend. The rank decides how much health it has, how hard it hits, how smart it fights and what it leaves behind. Consider shows the rank before the fight.
- Health, damage and armor now depend on rank and level, not just on whatever the area builder once typed in. Every respawn is a fresh roll.
- Veterans and up walk under sanctuary and fight with their heads: they curse you, strip your protection, save their strength for later. They make mistakes too: they stumble or get distracted.
- Bring good gear against a veteran or a champion. A boss or a legend falls either to the best gear and full preparation, or to a group.
- Higher rank, richer loot: champions, bosses and legends are guaranteed to leave every hero something worthwhile once a day.
- Every race now has its own body. Signature tricks stayed (a dragon's tail, a ghost that hits the whole room), while dodge or speed now come from rank.
- The rebuild started shops and saved mobs from scratch: their stock and items were reset.
Full help: mob ranks.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1791223596.subject: Diggers, swamps, parry, practices
1791223596.text:
The shovel now digs with the same chance everywhere, and the terrain decides what you find. In the shallows you pan sand, in deep water you dive to the bottom, and you can now dig in caves, volcanoes and underground rivers. No digging indoors or in the sewers.
- 28 rooms became real swamps with swamp water: murky, worse at quenching thirst, and a sip sometimes brings a mild plague.

Mobs no longer parry every blow: their chance is now that of a player with the skill at 100%. Heavy and two-handed weapons, and big unarmed fighters, are harder to parry.
- Flaming weapons blind only once in ten hits and only until the next tick, and gear heats up half as much.
- Vampiric weapons heal as much as they drank, not double that, and drop from corpses only for evil characters.
- Pets follow the same weapon weight rules you do.

The questor sells practices: quest buy practice gives 10 for 100 qp.

For crafters:
- Blueprint lists are clickable, and a failed craft ruins only one random ingredient, with luck counting here too. Missing a part you could make in the cuisinart? The game will tell you.
- Gems of other cuts, like the eastern sapphire, count as plain ones in blueprints. Thanks, Wolfram!
- The Artificers' parts cabinet holds only components, and masters craft from it first. The Artificers' Hall has an eternal steam forge, and the multitool digs, drills and chops faster.
- The salve for removing tattoos is now single-use.
- Constellations got stronger: Eclipse gives more health, protection and speed, Crystal more health, and Destruction adds damage too.

And smaller things:
- The sage shows what the score is made of and decides between a shield and a second weapon.
- Consider tells you whether a mob is sentient, and wisdom may stop you on the threshold of a deadly trap.
- Sentient pets recall with you, and affects shows how long a summoned one has left.
- Items dropped in shallow water settle on the bottom instead of sinking.
- Clan bank gold only at a bank or an ATM.
- The patron's luck now works for every class.
- Mobs below level 15 don't regain health in combat, and the living mold in Galeon went easier on newbies.
- With fightspam off, ranged spells get summed up like melee hits.
- The web client keeps your equipment script on your account, so all your characters have it.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1791509232.subject: Mob ranks, a tax-free bank, pets
1791509232.text:
Mob ranks got rules of their own, and dirty tricks no longer work on the strong ones. It's all in the help on mob ranks.
- A champion, boss or legend can't be charmed, summoned or thrown out of its lair. Instant kills, sleep, sconce and paralysis don't work on a boss or a legend, and a vorpal weapon fails only against a legend.
- Poison, plague and blindness wear off them sooner. A boss doesn't burn in a blaze, and a veteran or stronger remembers who set the fire and comes for them.
- Mobs get their dispelled spells back about twenty seconds after a fight, but never in the middle of one.
- Experience and gold depend on rank too: less from weaklings, plenty from champions and bosses.
- Guaranteed weapons and armor drop only from foes no lower in level than you.
- Kill and theft quests sometimes hand you a boss, and a boss sometimes turns up among the kidnappers.

Hundreds of ordinary items in the world now have random properties: an item keeps its own name but shows up with a fresh roll on top of its own stats every time. What you already own won't change. Details in the help on random items.

Login taxes are gone: neither the Sultan nor your purse eats your gold anymore. The shared account bank holds 10000 more gold for every character, and the bank no longer takes limited items.

- Pets wear your items, and saved and charmed ones no longer vanish at reboot along with their gear. The automaton folds back into its chassis if you say deactivate to it.
- Hero items got cheaper, down to 500 qp, and the quest bag can be upgraded too.
- The jeweler sets stones into random items as well, and forged armor now has a metal character: mithril and adamantite turn out differently.
- Liturgy: the better your skill, the less often your god gets angry, and at 100% never.
- New limits: the Sceptre of Chaos and the sanctuary bracer are now two per world, and the olive tiara just one, but it grants camouflage. Existing copies of these items were removed.
- Limited items no longer get stuck where nobody can find them again.
- The sage takes into account the skills an item teaches.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792031068.subject: Boss phases, the Kingdom of Mirrors, shield block, crafting
1792031068.text:
Bosses now fight in three phases, champions in two. Below 60% health a boss knocks down and disarms the tank, blinds casters, strips buffs and calls for help. Below 30% it panics and swings blind. Each phase opens with a scene.

The Dark Tower of the Kingdom of Mirrors is now taken by force: the Masters stand and fight, every slain Master opens the hatch to the next floor, and a boss waits at the top. The sword Taliesin and the Shield of the Rising Sun are now legendary, and the sword is always sharp, shocking and holy.

Every class can now learn shield block, and a shield catches even skill and spell hits. A heavy weapon can split a shield, and a shield can break a weapon.

- Every item in the world now has a real weight and price.
- Charmed followers now get set bonuses. When you quit they pack their gear into their bag and put it back on when you return. Your pet wears nothing.
- A crafted item's level and power now come from its blueprint: rare from level 30, epic from 45, legendary from 60. Sets got consistent names.
- Every new craft level gives 100 experience, and craft refit re-forges an item to your current level.
- Inks are made from pigments, a design's complexity is the tattooist level it needs, and carpenters get a new Wooden Soldier set.
- The tome of recipes now shows one table with a filter and holds 150 pages, and craft hides the Artificers' kit upgrade tiers you already passed.
- Scrap metal is melted down in a clay crucible, and arrows can be made from plain sticks.
- Tracks now show through portals. Thanks, Oof, Flanur, Zodd and Tio!
- Breath and crush from weak mobs no longer one-shot newbies, and you can jab an enemy with a torch.
- The questor suggests two available area quests, and quest list shows your quest points. Thanks, John!
- Dodge and parry cost less below level 50.
- A weapon you parry with is rarely chipped by a harder, heavier weapon, and a bow you parry with gets chipped every time.
- The replay command shows when each message arrived.
- You can cancel newbie quests you have outgrown, and the newbie channel is now the same as ooc.
- Clan guards recover when no enemy is around for a while.
- Nightfall snuffs out faerie fire in the room, and a hungry caster eats freshly created food at once.
- In the web client, blindness now slowly "breathes" instead of flashing (thanks, Kerrad!), and settings have triggers and MSP sounds.
- The Mudlet package moved to GMCP: health, prompt, chat, and a mapper with a starter map.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792241840.subject: Boss teeth, beast claws, raid loot
1792241840.text:
Bosses grew teeth. 61 bosses and legends now have a signature move of their own and their own scenes when the fight changes phase: one calls in servants, one hides under its shell, one throws the hero right out of its lair. Bosses and legends hit more often, and the ones that don't cast sometimes break through both shield and parry. Bosses and legends know no fear.

- Veterans and stronger casters fight smart: the necromancer curses first, healers and casters get silenced, sanctuary is the first thing to go, and the caster's pet won't be forgotten either.
- Beasts fight with what nature gave them: claws tear you bloody, fangs sink in, hooves trample the fallen, a snake squeezes so you can't flee, a spider wraps you in web, and a tail knocks you off your feet.
- Thief mobs knock you out and stab you in the back, vampires bite and heal, a ninja strangles and once in a while snaps a neck, and a druid casts its own spells.
- A ranger without a bow gets a random bow, a thief without a dagger gets a dagger, even if there's an axe or a club in its pack. That weapon drops like any ordinary random weapon.
- Hundreds of mobs got real classes, and 95 moved up in rank to veteran, champion or boss.
- Sentient mobs pick items up off the floor and wear them if they fit. Don't drop your gear next to a guard: he'll wear it on duty.
- Identical mobs now stand up for each other.
- Shopkeepers and servants became veterans and don't chase whoever hurt them, and shopkeepers also leave nothing behind when they die.
- A champion or stronger runs at the archer, and a veteran or stronger that can't reach you heals up and goes home. Thanks, Zodd!

Loot from champions, bosses and legends is now shared: in a group, everyone who dealt at least 15% of the damage gets a share of their own, once a day. The questor offers a new task, Boss Hunt, and the gang leader drops boss loot.
- Blueprints drop only from enemies of your level or higher.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792292376.subject: Crafting turns into a gamble, infravision, farewell to the orb
1792292376.text:
Crafting got a gambler's streak. Rare, epic and legendary pieces now roll random properties just like loot, and once in a while you get a masterpiece, one tier higher. craft reroll rerolls the random part. Any legendary item can be broken back down into materials, and epic metal ones sometimes give a scarce part too. Timers on rare and stronger items, crafted and looted alike, are now counted in days and are half as long. The top craft levels are harder to reach.

- New blueprints: garnet ring and garnet pendant, dreamcatcher, leather whip, travel cloak, leather gloves and iron horseshoes. Repair now eats a bit of material.
- Applying a tattoo now gives experience the way crafting does, legendary tattoo designs got rebalanced, and ink components are now sold in shops.
- Tattoos, gear and jeweler constellations that grant hide or sneak now keep it up for good. Before, it fell off after your first step.
- Stones in sockets survive their item decaying, and get a chance to survive when the item shatters or melts.

The crystal orb has retired: world news now reaches everyone, and who shows how many people are online.

With infravision, a dark room you see only by its heat now shows its name in red, and the pair of glowing eyes no longer gives away someone invisible or hidden. Dark vision is gone, but around 174 mobs can now see in the dark.

- Event sounds in the web client and over MSP: hits, low health, blindness, poison, tells, combat. See help sounds.
- Mudlet: no stray line after the prompt, the map shows up right after a reconnect, and Discord shows "Playing DreamLand".
- A drink cures hunger, put 3*sword puts exactly three, remove 2.necklace takes off the second necklace.
- examine on a container shows its description, run no longer goes in circles, and /who works.
- quest list is split into sections with links to help.
- Pegasi can be ridden, and newbies get a free canoe when they leave the Galeon.
- Golems and steam automatons survive their master's death, gear and all.
- The Rainbow Tower doors open for anyone who finished its quest. Vorpal no longer beheads bosses.
- The lessons command is replaced by help lessons. Timestamps in replay were Fils's idea, thank you!

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792673695.subject: Pets, legends, jewelry
1792673695.text:
Pets got smarter. In a fight they cast on their own, attack spells at your enemy included, and a beast pet goes at it with claws and teeth. A pet's price now follows its strength, the strongest ones exist one per world, and rats are sold only to characters in their first life. Pets that grow along with you have noticeably less health past level 80, but hit harder. The summoned demon got tougher too.

Legends can take a hit now: lag and daze from other people's skills wear off several times faster on them, scream no longer breaks their fight, and a shock cramp no longer makes them drop their weapon. A legend's death is now announced on the news channel, Telegram and Discord.

Mobs fight with the weapons of their class: swords, spears, maces and the other professional weapons are handled well only by those trained in them, everyone else handles them at half skill. Strong thieves hide, vampires fear light, silver and holy power, every dragon breathes, and clan guards fight like bosses of their rank. When a boss shifts phase, the web client flashes.

Jewelry got more even. Jeweler's pieces are now one per slot per tier, bracelets and masks joined the set, and three old rings are no longer made. Masks now take stones, and constellations gained level 20 pairs: thorn, dawn and owl. The power constellation now goes on one-handed weapons, and if a constellation no longer fits its item, the stones come back to you at login.

- New newbie quest in Midgaard, "Hide-and-Seek": a kid on Temple Square asks you to find an invisible friend and a hidden one.
- Mobs no longer grab a weapon or shield knocked out of your hands: you get 30 seconds to pick it up.
- Mastering sword works only with a katana. In return, samurai shrug off boss fear and stand firmer when they get pushed or hurled.
- Boss Hunt offers only bosses you can actually reach, and bosses below your level drop no loot. Vampiric touch no longer puts bosses and legends to sleep.
- The nishtyak, the artifact and the cap of invisibility from the shop in The Hut are ten times cheaper now, but they're worn only in your first life.
- Infravision paints the name of a dark room red, not the creatures in it.
- nuke all works again, and the skeleton a necromancer raises no longer comes up as a training dummy. Thanks, Zodd!

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792810202.subject: Shops, pets, samurai
1792810202.text:
We rewrote shops from scratch. When a room has several shopkeepers, all of them serve you: list shows their goods as one list, numbered straight through, sell takes each item to whoever pays the most, and sell sword from Hans sends the sword to Hans. A full shop no longer says it has nowhere to put the goods.

- Changed your mind after a sale? For 10 minutes the shopkeeper keeps the item for you: buy back returns it for the same price.
- sell junk sells the junk: trash and gear that does nothing for you by the sages' measure. value junk shows first what would go.
- The list shows from which level an item fits you, when it is not for your alignment, or when you can't wear it at all. Newbies also see whether armor is better than what they wear.
- inspect shows an item's properties. Say a row number out loud and the shopkeeper tells you about the item.
- Some shops keep hours, and a closed one tells you when it opens.
- Sold random items don't go back on the shelves, and shops restock what they are meant to sell.
- Shops started counting what people buy and sell. Soon prices will follow demand.

A living shopkeeper now sells pets in the pet shop: they come after the goods in his list, priced by strength, you can haggle, and on the day of big discounts they cost half. Ten pet shops that had no seller now have one, and Nabil in New Thalos sells exotic critters: a scarab, a hawk and a gecko.

Samurai got a way of their own. iaido replaces counter and cuts straight from the sheath as the fight starts, kaeshi answers a parry with a strike, and tameshigiri is a test cut across the whole room that replaces explode and catches the unseen too. bushido is both fudoshin (the less health you have, the harder you hit) and zanshin (a strike at an unseen enemy who comes back). An ashigaru serves you and becomes your kaishakunin at harakiri. Without one, death costs more.

- You can give your katana a name, and it now grows without the mastering sword skill, only three times slower.
- Samurai learn cleave from level 50.
- A masterful cross block gives a free try at weapon cleave or disarm, and a bad one tangles you up.

- tell to a mob in the same room works like say: quests hear it. Thanks, Cryo!
- Items with combat effects no longer fire twice per round.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1792897492.subject: Achievements and player profiles
1792897492.text:
DreamLand now has achievements, more than three hundred of them. Quests, fights, bosses, crafting, rebirths, clan business, and secrets nobody will tell you about. Each one has a tier: common, rare, epic or legendary. Titles are not forever: you stay the Bounty King only until someone beats your count.

Old deeds are already counted for everyone, retroactively. Type achievements to see yours, and whois shows the latest five.

Newbies earn achievements too, they just don't get a public page yet.

The public profile at dreamland.rocks/player/<name> shows every achievement and every character on the account. It exists only for players with an account, meaning a linked Telegram or Discord. It opens once any character on the account has been reborn or finished more than 50 questor tasks.

Heads up: the public page lists every character on the account with its class, so your alts' classes are no longer much of a secret. Want to stay out of sight? account profile off takes the page down, account profile hide <name> hides one character.

More in the in-game help: help achievements.

1793276842.subject: Prices, use, help
1793276842.text:
Shop prices now follow demand: what players buy a lot slowly gets pricier, what they sell a lot gets cheaper. The shift is at most a tenth of the price and no more than two percent a day, and such goods are marked in the list. Items up to level 10 never get pricier, and the shopkeeper takes back what you bought for no more than nine tenths of the price.

Potions, scrolls, wands and staves are now all used with one command, use. quaff, recite, zap and brandish went into retirement. Battleragers get herbal pills for every rank. Staves became their own weapon class, with the staff skill: 17 staves moved over from spears, and your spear skill carries over to staff by itself when you log in.

Help got smarter. It searches by every word, suggests similar articles, tells you where to look when you type the name of an area, mob or item, and every article ends with "See also". You can also plug it into your AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT and so on) as an MCP server: https://dreamland.rocks/mcp/help

- The katana grows with its owner: every time it glows, its level and damage dice catch up with your level.
- Carpenters make the legendary Grove Warden set.
- Bosses have elemental immunities, and their legendary items carry the boss's name. Five more area rulers became bosses, and Boss Hunt offers targets from 5 levels below you to 10 above.
- Random items roll properties in a new way: how many you get is random, and penalties happen too.
- A pet's report says how much it grew in your service, and say with a number in the pet shop shows the report for that pet. Thanks, Tio!
- The bonus panther no longer takes a follower slot. throw aims like a ranged spell.
- You can link an alt to your account with a code right in the game, no email needed.
- where merchant, where blacksmith or where sage finds the mob you need. Thanks, Zodd!
- Mobs above level 103 hold weapons you can actually wear. The Nagelring got stronger.
- Legends and bosses don't drop their weapon to shock cramp.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1793365925.subject: Magic items, staves, leaderboards
1793365925.text:
Magic items got reworked. They now drop from enemies, just like random items: mages, clerics and necromancers more often leave scrolls and charged trinkets, everyone else leaves pills and potions. Champions, bosses and legends always carry magic, chests hold it too, and locked chests hold better. The higher the tier, the more spells an item has and the sooner it crumbles. From the rare tier up, rings, amulets, gloves and lights can carry spell charges too, and you use them with the use command. Many old potions, pills, scrolls and wands got new spells and charges, and the copies you already own changed with them. Shops sell only common and uncommon magic.

Staves now cast through the staff skill, and a targeted spell hits a single target, like a wand, not the whole room. A staff held in both hands parries well, and carpenters make battle staves. Shalafi mages got imbue: put your own spell into a staff or an item in your hand, and mastering staff sometimes wakes that spell with a blow.

Item timers and affects now keep running while you're out of the game. Come back after a long break and some of your items will have crumbled, and the spells on you and your gear will have worn off. Curses and other debuffs don't wear off while you're away.

The website has leaderboards now: achievements, remorts, quests, bosses, crafting, travel and even deaths, plus who plays what over the last month. Take a look: https://dreamland.rocks/leaderboard.html

- Anti-paladin ranks are cheaper: the initiation takes 150 kills and 100 qp.
- worth now shows score, and kills and deaths sit at the very end of score.
- Quest bandits are always of the alignment opposite to yours.
- Quest mobs see in the dark and see the invisible.
- Mage and cleric mobs regain mana faster, and charmed vampires and paladins obey order cast.
- A kill with gear heated red-hot is now credited to whoever heated it. You can burn your own empty corpse.
- James Joyce is back with the Battleragers: he cleans the cave.
- Correction: bosses did not get elemental immunities. Immunity to a boss's element can roll on its legendary item.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1793490219.subject: Armor, bosses, bleeding
1793490219.text:
Armor is finally fixed, only 30 years late.

- Armor no longer makes you harder to hit. It soaks part of a blow that lands, up to 60 percent. Higher armor is better, and score shows it as positive numbers.
- Accuracy (hitroll) pierces armor. Dexterity and level help you avoid hits. Holy, negative and mental damage ignore armor.
- Armor types now really differ.
- Jewelers repair jewelry and treasure.
- Mob damage and stats are rebalanced around the new armor.
- Fixed bosses: they now act in every phase of the fight, as they always should have.
- Fixed: raid pets were untouchable for bosses and took turns keeping them on the ground.
- 23 zone leaders that were meant to be bosses finally are.
- Critical hits open a bleeding wound, and while it bleeds your body doesn't heal. Bandage is now for everyone.
- Without the swim skill you can dive on the second try, but underwater without gills you drown.
- Your first attack on a groupmate asks for confirmation.
- Screen reader mode tells you how much experience is left to the next level after every gain.
- run unlocks doors with a key you carry and stops if your party falls behind.
- config twohands: a two-handed weapon takes your shield off by itself.
- config noautoblood: a vampire doesn't drink from the kill.
- look at an item shows the same as a click in the web client, and examine reads the details. Thanks, Tahi!
- Item damage from acid, fire and cold is now visible to the owner. Thanks, Tio!
- Quests no longer send you into deep water, mid-air or traps.
- Clan guards let allies through.
- NPC followers sit, rest and sleep together with you.
- The prompt has %b and %B: carried and maximum weight.
- Energy drain gives the caster the victim's mana instead of moves.
- Gear sages got even smarter and know better what you need.
- Newbies get a hint to practice a skill that keeps failing.
- Felines hunt bats.
- Ask the ashigaru and he brings a cup of sake, and for three silver he fetches a bottle.
- A fire death in PK leaves an urn of ashes.
- auction talk is gone, chat in ooc or ic.
- The pneumatic post periscope turns in any direction to peek into the next room.
- The help MCP for your AI assistant now also searches items, sees who is online and reads the news: https://dreamland.rocks/mcp/help

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1793632004.subject: Saving throws, item wear, achievements
1793632004.text:
Saving throws against spells have been reworked. Against a caster of your own level you now start at 40% to resist, and every level of difference adds or takes away 3%. Saves vs spell work with diminishing returns: the first points matter most. Your chance never drops below 5% and never goes above 90%. A made save always protects you from deadly spells, and a failed one is not death yet: there is a second roll. Cancellation and dispel affects follow a soft curve too. Score shows your chance to resist and how much damage your armor stops, and identify shows how an item changes that.

Item wear finally matters. Every full 10 points of lost condition costs 5% of an item's armor. The more worn a weapon is, the weaker it hits, and a sharp blade below 50 condition goes blunt until repaired. Items with no value don't wear.

Thirty or so new achievements, and help now knows all of them, plus class level titles, clan ranks and player names.

- Snowballs are back: in winter, snowfall piles up drifts, and you can pack snowballs from them and throw them at your neighbour.
- Underwater, spells fail almost every other time, since neither voice nor hands obey. No mana is lost, and gills don't help.
- get understands multi-word item and container names without quotes.
- write can copy and paste paper sections through the editor.
- fill with no target leaves puddles and portable containers on the floor alone.
- vomit leaves a puddle of swill.
- Jewelers ask you to confirm a repair and forget the quote after 5 minutes. Coal tongs save you from burns at the forge.
- A witch curse that doesn't land tires the caster for a tick.
- Energy drain and hand of undead heal the caster for the damage dealt, not the damage rolled.
- New set "Dancing in Jeans" for the dove and the jeans from Sad Songs and Waltzes.
- With fightspam off, the fight summary prints one line per victim.
- Identify folds identical bonuses into one line and marks a blunted sharp blade in gray.
- Arcadian words turn water into wine and beer in fountains too, from 50 mastery.
- The carpenter's wooden bracelet can be crafted again.
- The scroll of knowledge recognises its owner after a remort.
- Cooldown timers in affects are magenta, like in the web client.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1793867908.subject: Races, remorts, racial crafts
1793867908.text:
Every race in Dreamland has been rebalanced. We priced each one on the same ruler: stats, resistances, vulnerabilities, racial skills. The races that sat at the bottom for years (half-elves, githyanki, kenders, hobbits, drow) now stand next to the favourites. The ones that were too fat (svirfnebli, dwarves, faeries, gnomes, storm giants) lost some weight.

- New stats, resistances, vulnerabilities and racial skills for many races: some added, some taken away. Check your race's help to see what changed for you.
- Elves are now wise rather than clever: a race for clerics. Githyanki are strong and sharp: a race for anti-paladins and vampires.
- If your race lost a stat point, the trains you put into it come back to you at login.
- A remort bonus now lifts a stat at most 3 points above your race and class limit (5 for humans), and never above 28. Anyone who bought more gets the extra back and wakes up in Baba Yaga's hut to spend it again. For your main stat this is often a plus: remorts used to stop at 25.

Racial crafts:
- Dwarves are born blacksmiths, elves carpenters, svirfnebli jewelers: their work turns out masterworks more often.
- A tattoo a satyr inks with their own ink lasts twice as long.
- The gear sage gives gnomes advice for free.

And bad news for faeries: cold iron. A faery who wears or wields anything made of iron or steel cannot blink. The Secret of the Sidhe set saves them.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1794006971.subject: Gods' gifts, archers, blind players
1794006971.text:
All 33 gods' gifts have been reworked: every mark now weighs about the same, and the gods who gave next to nothing for years finally give something. Most gifts work all the time instead of once every hundred blows, and many gods open a fight with a spell of their own. Read your god's help to see what yours gives. Siebele and Alala accept only women, Turlok only men. You can renounce your religion once per life, and score shows it.

The bow hits more often and wears only on a fumbled shot. You can also shoot point-blank, in your own room: it's harder to hit, and a mob you miss comes straight at you.

For blind players: who, skills and exits read one line per entry, and races and classes in who are declined properly. The map in the web client can be walked from the keyboard and has a room list, Tab reads the game output, Alt plus arrows reads chat. New players can dictate commands by voice and pick menu items by number.

- The Arena is its own zone now: PK there doesn't make you a killer and doesn't count toward stats, rating or ears.
- A remort raises a stat at most 3 above its training cap (5 for humans). Anything above that comes back as points at Baba Yaga's hut. Races got reworked too: resistances, vulnerabilities, skills, crafts.
- A clan relic can be sacrificed again. The gods won't forget it, and neither will the clan.
- Global quests end on time and show a standings table at the end, gangsters come in different races, and their chief is a real boss.
- Elites walk up to a sniper anywhere inside their own zone.
- config numbers: damage numbers have their own toggle.
- get takes items with multi-word names without quotes.
- socials rus sorts the list by Russian names.
- Pets that a boss threw off stay yours.
- Repair strips corrosion, and reworking a masterpiece keeps its rarity.
- Groupmates see what's in the corpse on a kill, and a vampire stands up after digging out of a grave.
- The shop list shows where an item is worn. Shops that buy potions buy pills too.
- Legends and bosses from level 45 have more health, a quarter more from level 65.
- Vampiric weapons tell their owner how much health they drained.
- Farsight always shows the exits of the distant room.
- Ghosts are now hurt by light, and holy still hurts them most.
- Lots of lines that only spoke Russian now speak your language.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1794232191.subject: Mob defenses, whips, web client
1794232191.text:
Champions, bosses and legends now have defenses of their own: a few random resistances, a chance of an immunity for bosses and legends, and a vulnerability on top for legends. The set reshuffles every month, so it pays to consider a mob before a fight: consider now tells you what it is immune, resistant and vulnerable to. Unarmed, these mobs alternate ordinary blows with blows of their own element.

The web client got a pile of new things, mostly for blind players: game lists in a window with buttons, exit and room sounds, reading and searching the output, area and item search, the game guide and routes from the Market Square, settings pages for screen readers, an easier login and better phone support. The # commands speak your language. Thanks, OlegTheSnowman!

- Aggressive mobs no longer jump anyone more than 20 levels below them, and thief and ninja ambushes leave alone anyone more than 10 below.
- Mob thieves blackjack a sleeper first, then backstab.
- Whips and flails are still hard to parry, but now it can be done, and then they may tangle the weapon. If the wielder wins the pull, the defender is left empty-handed. If the wielder loses, they lose their own weapon, and a sharp blade cuts the whip through on top of that.
- Flood: the ground turns into shallow water, then deep water, and the water drains away if the ritual is interrupted. Thanks, Bromir!
- Boss and legend loot timers show up in quest trophies, consider and the questor's hint, and the timer starts only on a kill that paid out. Boss Hunt no longer refuses because of an unreachable lair.
- Saves now show everywhere as your chance to resist, in percent.
- Bow shots and thrown weapons show when the target is AFK or link-dead. Thanks, Miyamoto!
- The recipe tome tells you how to open its index, and the links work for a tome lying on the floor. Thanks, Hinore!
- Midgaard now has a bone needle and thimbles of wood and bone. Thanks, Lesmyavka!
- Blindness, venom and webs from beasts are no longer spells but physical effects with a resist roll. The kender trades hide for blindness dust.
- The skill pair from the marks of Dwarkin and Tirna holds for a day instead of changing on every login. A few gods' marks got stronger.
- Stats of the faery, arial, dark-elf, githyanki and felar got a lift.
- Legendary armor now drops as jewelry and clothing too.
- New social: pet, for animals. Cats respond to it.
- Jewelers offer repair in the web client menus, and pets bought in shops keep their level.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!

1794570754.subject: Booze and drugs, warrior subclasses, dreams
1794570754.text:
You can now drink, smoke and more in Thera. Booze goes to your head in stages of drunkenness and pays you back in the morning with a hangover. A fisstech peddler comes out at night, shops stock weed, tobacco and opium for casters, and mushrooms grow in forests and caves, fly agaric for berserkers among them. Drinkers and smokers now smell of it, and the city guard pats your pockets for fisstech.

Warrior subclasses are open: from level 20 the guildmaster in Midgaard takes you to the trial, and the blood picks your path.
- Fencer: one sword, precision, and the point where the armor isn't.
- Berserker: a weapon in each hand and a rage that grows the closer you are to death.
- Sentinel: a shield the enemy wounds himself on.

Dreams now come in order, the unseen ones first, and dream list and dream read open them like mail. Who dreamed them up stays a secret.

- The hero weapon is bought by naming its kind, and reshaped into another kind for quest points.
- Haste, rally, bat swarm and holy armor can no longer be cast mid-fight, like every other buff.
- Bladestorm spins over several combat rounds, and fleeing can tear webs and brambles.
- Creativity raises the odds of a masterwork, and with it or with Prometheus a failed craft doesn't eat the materials. A legendary masterwork gets one more property.
- A fully mastered ranger staff makes a tier-two staff (thanks, Inis!), and Arancus's druid staff became a real weapon.
- The mana blessing now also cuts the movement cost of skills. Thanks, Eleonor!
- Killing a wanted player or a thief earns the city's loyalty.
- Satyrs and followers of Cradya and Bastian create wine or beer instead of water.
- A blacksmith samurai's katana no longer crumbles, and vampires learn energy drain at level 35.
- A newbie who puts on an item sees what it gives, and a naked one gets new gear from the dwarf on the Galeon's deck.
- exits shows each exit's description, group reads one sentence per member in screen reader mode, and screen readers skip decorative symbols in item names.
- A written sheet of paper reads itself when you pick it up, and scan says when nobody is around.
- The area quest cooldown shows how many minutes are left.
- The game warns you before the world freezes for a reload.
- Plenty of items that had no reset spawn in their zones again.

As always, thanks to everyone who tests new features and reports bugs!
